metadata.source: Bhikkhu Pāsādika and Bhikkhu Tampalawela Dhammaratana: Contemporary Sri Lankan Sanskrit Poetry: The Yaśodharācaritam by Davuldeṇa Jñāneśvara Mahāsthavira. Bulletin d'etudes indienne 21.1 (2003), pp. 47-70.

children.translated_text: The glorious <s>Siddhārtha</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> in <s>Kapilavastu</s>, [leaving] his wife with their son,
and the queen, abandoning all wealth and the glory of a universal monarch,
in the month of <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, on the full-moon night, with a mind turned away [from worldly life],
departed, bearing the status of a wandering ascetic (<s>śramaṇa</s>), desiring to seek liberation. // Yaśo_1 //
Then at dawn, having risen from her bed,
the queen <s>Yaśodharā</s>, together with her son,
with eagerness to see her beloved lord, swiftly
went to the bedchamber nearby. // Yaśo_2 //

children.text: yathā pure vañcayituṃ sa me patī
children.translated_text: 'Just as before, my husband has gone somewhere hidden to deceive me'—
[thinking] he was concealed in some secret place—
searching intensely inside and outside the palace,
examining everywhere, she did not see him at all. // Yaśo_3 //
She then rushed to the minister's residence,
flinging open the lattice window, running faster and faster in her anguish,
striking the door firmly again and again,

children.text: vyarīravac channa bhavan bhavann iti || Yaśo_4 ||
children.translated_text: she cried out, 'O <s>Channa</s>! O lord! O lord!' // Yaśo_4 //

children.text: apekṣya kiṃ cit kvaṇam antarād gṛhe
children.translated_text: Hearing some slight sound from within the house,
she stood for a moment near the doorkeeper;
sighing as her deliberation was shattered, with her hand
she struck both her cheeks. // Yaśo_5 //
Then she went to the royal horse-stable;
she did not see the horse <s>Kanthaka</s> there.

children.text: kuto yayau kiṃ rahasā sa vallabho
children.translated_text: 'Where has my beloved gone, and why secretly?'—
speculating thus, she fell into a faint. // Yaśo_6 //

children.text: vicintya yat kiṃ cid itas tataḥ śiraś
children.translated_text: Thinking various thoughts, turning her head this way and that,

children.text: cacāla jaghrau ca mukhe sutasya sā |
children.translated_text: she smelled her son's face;
with the canopy of her arm, from her two eyes
she held back the spray of flowing tears. // Yaśo_7 //
Unable to endure at all the rising
anguish of mind, with fierce anger,
the jeweled neck-ornament given by her husband,
the coral garland, and the pair of earrings, // Yaśo_8 //
the forehead ornament, the golden ring,
the girdle fastened with a golden cord—
removing the head-ornament and the bracelets,

children.text: sasarja dhig dhig vadatī sasambhramam || Yaśo_9 ||
children.translated_text: she cast them away, exclaiming 'Alas! Alas!' in agitation. // Yaśo_9 //
She struck the ground with the sole of her foot,
yawned, stretched upward, and tore her hair;
she spoke words confused and devoid of meaning,
wailed as if terrified, and wept with choking sobs. // Yaśo_10 //
Placing the child on the bed again and again,
throwing up both hands simultaneously,
shaking her head as if unconscious,
she shrieked, gasped, fell down, and trembled. // Yaśo_11 //
Though constantly oppressed by hunger,

children.text: na bhojanaṃ bhoktum iyeṣa kiṃ cana |
children.translated_text: she did not wish to eat any food at all;
though tormented by thirst, she did not drink even a drop of water,

children.text: papau ca kāye 'py babhūva vepathuḥ || Yaśo_12 ||
children.translated_text: and a trembling came over her body. // Yaśo_12 //
Intellect, memory, vitality, and fortitude are destroyed,
bodily complexion, and strength in the senses too;
life gradually perishes—
such is the endless [suffering of] separation from the beloved. // Yaśo_13 //
Sitting on the ground with her body half-bent,
placing her head and both hands upon her lap,
bending her neck slightly,
she sank into the ocean of anxiety, without support. // Yaśo_14 //
'Because of the humiliating conduct of <s>Yaśodharā</s>,
unable to bear it, Prince <s>Siddhārtha</s>, all alone,
abandoned his dwelling and went to the forest'—

children.text: iti pravādo 'pi bhaved aho mama || Yaśo_15 ||
children.translated_text: such a rumor might arise about me, alas! // Yaśo_15 //

children.text: yad asti kāryaṃ triṣu mandireṣu tac
children.translated_text: Whatever duties there were in the three palaces,
I performed them as a capable and devoted servant should;

children.text: gatau sthitau vā śayane ca vipriyaṃ
children.translated_text: whether in walking, standing, or in bed, anything displeasing

children.text: kadā canāhaṃ na cakāra kiṃ cana || Yaśo_16 ||
children.translated_text: I never did at any time. // Yaśo_16 //
Reflecting on the sudden calamity that had befallen [her],
she proceeded to the temple, [praying] for her beloved;
with fragrant flowers, incense, and lamps,
she worshipped the assembly of gods with reverence. // Yaśo_17 //
Placing both arms upon her head, the grief-stricken woman,
gazing at the beautiful face of the divine image,
bowing with devotion and a purified mind,
implored the gods thus, [lamenting] the separation: // Yaśo_18 //
'You who are the causes of the creation, maintenance, and destruction of the three worlds—
<s>Caturmukha</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), <s>Śrīpati</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), and <s>Candraśekhara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>)—
O mighty lords of the universe, O gods,
be a refuge for me who am greatly afflicted!' // Yaśo_19 //
Having made this supplication, in the hands of the gods
she offered and tied coins as gifts;
she presented sweet fresh milk-rice,
a white cloth, and a golden doll. // Yaśo_20 //
To bring delight to the lords of the gods,
she caused bells to resound, and summoned Brahmins;
she had hymns of praise recited in divine language,

children.text: nanāma bhūmāv asakṛt nipatya sā || Yaśo_21 ||
children.translated_text: and bowed to the ground, prostrating repeatedly. // Yaśo_21 //
'Whether my beloved dwells in the city, in the forest, or in a hermitage—
wherever he may be—with [your] divine eye
look upon [him] and cause him to return home!'
Thus she continued to beseech the celestials. // Yaśo_22 //
Gazing with an unblinking, sidelong glance,
stamping her foot firmly on the ground,
repeatedly biting her tender lower lip,
emphatically raising and shaking her forefinger, // Yaśo_23 //
'Hey you! Have you not heard or seen

children.text: śruto na dṛṣṭaḥ vada kiṃ nirākulam |
children.translated_text: the departure of the noble one from the house? Speak without evasion!'
Thus she questioned the doorkeeper-guard
in a loud angry voice, her eyes brimming with tears. // Yaśo_24 //
'That one, O noble lady, the crest-jewel of the royal lineage—
he was not seen by me when he came to the gate for the watch.
With the noble ladies in the pleasure garden,
in the deep of night he sported—so I have heard.' // Yaśo_25 //
'The prince is surely not free from passion, is he?
Therefore he must have desired a new beloved!

children.text: mithaḥ sa kāṃ cit pariṇīya nāṭikāṃ
children.translated_text: Having secretly married some actress,
he has gone outside today—so I conjecture.' // Yaśo_26 //
'For in ancient times, the one renowned as <s>Māndhātṛ</s>,
he too, though a universal sovereign, among the hosts of celestial women
became enamored, and abandoning his earthly

children.text: śriyaṃ prapede nu divaukasāṃ puram || Yaśo_27 ||
children.translated_text: glory, went to the city of the gods. // Yaśo_27 //
'Leaving aside the mind-delighting troupe of celestial beauties,
at the hermitage of the ascetic in the <s>Vindhya</s> mountains,
embracing the ascetic wife of <s>Agastya</s>,
<s>Pākaśāsana</s> (<s>Indra</s>) dallied with her at night. // Yaśo_28 //
'The foremost of kings, the ten-headed one (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>),
having conquered <s>Laṅkā</s> renowned across the world, went to the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest,
and seizing <s>Sītā</s>, the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>,
made her his own, treating her as his own beloved. // Yaśo_29 //
'And the Great Lord (<s>Maheśvara</s>, <s>Śiva</s>) himself, formerly while performing austerities,
with <s>Umā</s> his queen in the pleasure-grove,
setting aside the cultivation of constant <s>samādhi</s>,
he sported and begot two sons, did he not? // Yaśo_30 //
To console the grief-stricken best of brides,
the doorkeeper, placing his palms together at his chest,
with a pleasant voice and compassion,
with bowed head, respectfully informed [her] with these words: // Yaśo_31 //
'Hey you! [Tell me] whether the noble one today
is in the house, outside, or in the garden—somewhere, anywhere,
at the beginning of day or at night—did you see [him]?'
Thus she questioned her own maidservant with anger. // Yaśo_32 //
Placing her left knee upon the other,
[resting] on the ground, with both arms upon her forehead,
the maidservant, with body half-bowed, declared:

children.text: śrutaṃ ca dṛṣṭaṃ na na vedmi kiṃ cana || Yaśo_33 ||
children.translated_text: 'Neither heard nor seen—I know nothing whatsoever.' // Yaśo_33 //
Thereupon, the virtuous woman, having gone up to the upper palace,
wiping the flowing tears from her eyes,
'Hey! Has the noble one come here or not?'
she asked the eunuch guard of the inner palace. // Yaśo_34 //
'With praiseworthy beauty, sweet speech,
and splendor as well as composure, [three women] have come to your chamber;
honored by all people in the highest [fashion],
his three beloved wives are they. // Yaśo_35 //
'You, the mind-delighting one, are <s>Bhāratī</s> (<s>Sarasvatī</s>);
and likewise <s>Lakṣmī</s>—such are his beloved wives.
The prince always delights with them;

children.text: kadā cid anyatra mano 'sya no rajet || Yaśo_36 ||
children.translated_text: his mind would never be captivated by another.' // Yaśo_36 //
'What is despised by wise and self-possessed noble men—
desire, which is full of faults—your husband is averse to it;
therefore, his movement within the inner palace

children.text: śrutā na dṛṣṭā na divā vā niśi || Yaśo_37 ||
children.translated_text: has been neither heard nor seen, by day or by night.' // Yaśo_37 //
'Having attained equality with the wealthy in austerities,

children.text: ratiṃ na kuryāt sa bhavatraye kva cit |
children.translated_text: he would not take pleasure anywhere in the three worlds;
in this prison-house, which is like a house of filth,

children.text: kathaṃ vidhatte ratim eṣa te patiḥ || Yaśo_38 ||
children.translated_text: how would your husband take delight?' // Yaśo_38 //
'In this body, which is a repository of incurable diseases, a house of misery,
a belly constantly oppressed by hunger,
that cannot be satisfied by various foods and drinks—

children.text: spṛhāṃ na dehe prakaroti paṇḍitaḥ || Yaśo_39 ||
children.translated_text: a wise man does not make [such] an attachment to the body.' // Yaśo_39 //
'Upon skin scattered with drops of hot perspiration,
decorated in various colors, fashioned with impurity—
seeing [such] a body, a person perishes
like a moth before the radiance of a blazing lamp-flame.' // Yaśo_40 //
Then, hearing the words spoken by the palace eunuch-guard,
<s>Yaśodharā</s>, having paid close attention to his speech,
to the royal garden, resembling the <s>Nandana</s> grove of the gods,
went with a restless mind. // Yaśo_41 //
Then the guardian of that beautiful garden,
approaching [her], with hands clasped at his chest,
'For what purpose, O noble lady, is your arrival here?'
he announced, "I wish to inquire." // Yaśo_42 //
"O friend, has my noble lord in secret at sunrise
come here or has he not come?

children.text: kim atra dṛṣṭaḥ sa na vā śrutas tvayā
children.translated_text: Was he seen here, or was he not heard of by you?

children.text: vicintya samyag vada māṃ yathātatham || Yaśo_43 ||
children.translated_text: Consider well and tell me the truth." // Yaśo_43 //
"The noble son, free from desire for the five objects of sense-pleasure,
has become one who has conquered his senses.
Therefore, a visit to this delightful park

children.text: na dṛṣṭa ārye na hi vā śruto mayā || Yaśo_44 ||
children.translated_text: has neither been seen nor heard of by me regarding the noble one." // Yaśo_44 //
Wishing to bring about the welfare of the three worlds,
having heard the supplication of the celestial beings,
he descended from heaven by the power of his merit
and was born in a human birth, that Lord. // Yaśo_45 //
When the great celebration was taking place, the sage <s>Asita</s> had gone

children.text: divaṃ kim ity asya vimṛśya kāraṇam |
children.translated_text: to heaven—reflecting on the reason for this,
"A son is born to his friend King <s>Śuddhodana</s>!"
—out of joy, he went to see him. // Yaśo_46 //
Then the sage <s>Asita</s>, having arrived at the royal palace,
beholding the young prince endowed with the wealth of merit,
with a suprasensory eye made of knowledge,
examined the bodily marks of the child. // Yaśo_47 //
He spoke these words: "This child is meritorious;
he shall indeed become a <s>Buddha</s>, having destroyed the bonds of <s>Māra</s>.
He shall ferry across all men, gods, and demons
from the boundless great ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>." // Yaśo_48 //
Then, among the five <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, having examined the bodily marks,
the wise <s>Kauṇḍinya</s> spoke thus:
"Having destroyed the impurities of <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) and the like, this child
shall attain the unsurpassed state of <s>Buddhahood</s>." // Yaśo_49 //
Then, at the very moment of birth, in the grove of <s>Lumbinī</s>,
he walked upon the crowns of seven lotuses,
and roared a fearless cry across the three worlds:

children.text: bhaveyam agras tv iti siṃhapotavat || Yaśo_50 ||
children.translated_text: "I shall be the foremost!"—like a young lion. // Yaśo_50 //
With the enchanting sound of buzzing bees pleasing to the ears,
with masses of fragrant flower pollen,
a breeze mixed with the spray of rivers

children.text: vavau samantād vipine śanaiḥ tadā || Yaśo_51 ||
children.translated_text: blew gently on all sides through the grove at that time. // Yaśo_51 //
At the supremely magnificent birth of that great-souled one,
treasures arose from the earth.
The goddess of the earth, then exceedingly delighted,
displayed wondrous perfection upon the ground. // Yaśo_52 //
Thereupon, from the grove of <s>Lumbinī</s> to the home
resplendent like the orb of variegated gold,
the two affectionate parents brought the young prince
home, surrounded by the company of relatives. // Yaśo_53 //
The subjects prescribed by the teacher, and all the branches
of learning, systems, and philosophies—dear to his teacher,
by the power of merit accumulated over birth after birth,
this intelligent one mastered them all in a short time. // Yaśo_54 //
When this noble son had attained the splendor of fresh youth
through learning and steadfastness, from the time of his birth,
together with you, in the sixteenth year,
the marriage consecration was duly performed, was it not? // Yaśo_55 //
